# work-contract

## Do
Apply this contract within the authorized scope, regardless of entry skill or delegation. Receive/read applicable Do and Check guidance before the first product-source edit; reuse current guidance already available, and retrieve missing guidance before dependent work or completion. Skills supply methods, not exemptions. These instructions are not a host-enforced lock.

- Keep original requirements, accepted amendments, authority, scope and preserved behavior available. Do not narrow them to match the implementation. Conversation and existing artifacts suffice; no mandatory spec, approval round or evidence ledger.
- Preserve evidence before an action destroys it: reproduce a defined mismatch against its expected behavior before repair; characterize behavior/contracts before restructuring; retain the selected design reference. Existing valid tests and references suffice.
- Inspect relevant implementation and consumers. Prefer existing components or compatible extensions; keep responsibilities clear and avoid unnecessary duplication or generality. Validate inputs where they become trusted. Apply [dry](dry.md), [yagni](yagni.md), [kiss](kiss.md) and [boundary-validation](boundary-validation.md) to direct and delegated product work.
- Verify external dependency/API fields, parameters and behavior before relying on them. Resolve missing support before a dependent workaround. Obtain authority for an otherwise unauthorized persisted-data change or migration; routine reversible choices need no renewed approval.
- Repair the supported cause; preserve compatibility and ownership unless change is authorized. Use [root-cause](root-cause.md), [failing-test-first](failing-test-first.md) and [behavior-tests](behavior-tests.md) for investigation and proof. Do not duplicate a valid reproduction merely to create a new test.
- Before implementing changed UI/interactions, establish a checked reference covering the requirements; use preview for missing coverage and reuse an accepted reference. Proposal-only work does not authorize product edits. Narrow copy/comment/constant corrections without behavior or contract changes need repo verification and diff inspection, not a new proposal or full workflow.
- Choose methods for the next action, including after findings within a turn. Apply newly relevant guidance before dependent work without waiting for another message or changing an exclusive task label. Reuse settled decisions and completed work that still apply.
- Resolve consequential missing requirements or authority before dependent actions; continue independent authorized work. Keep read-only and tests-only assignments within scope: discovering a defect does not authorize repair. Performance measurement requires an explicit user request.
- Delegate when useful, with original requirements, preserved contracts, ownership, relevant source/evidence and complete applicable guidance, including this contract. Workers choose methods within scope; the main owns integration and completion. No fixed agent sequence.

## Check
- Reconcile original requirements and accepted amendments with actual work, including capabilities absent from the diff. For each claim, inspect the command/interaction, conditions, expected and observed result, relevant version, inputs/state, environment and coverage.
- Satisfy repo verification and relevant changed-file tests on the final relevant state, within ownership and forbidden-command rules. Inspect executed assertions and behavior. A name, exit zero, zero tests, all-skipped run, setting or worker PASS is not proof. Broaden checks only for an authorized task-specific reason.
- Apply all relevant evidence conditions:
  - New/changed behavior: required outcomes and relevant exceptions.
  - Bug repair: the same trigger failing for the actual defect before repair and passing afterward, plus preservation checks.
  - Restructuring: promised behavior and external contracts remain intact.
  - UI/interactions: compare the actual implemented screen with the selected reference at relevant sizes/states, exercise affected connected flows and inspect rendered images. Prototype/model tests do not verify unexecuted product interactions.
  - API-only work: inspect a real changed handler/service response, its status, fields and contract, not only mocks. Use [real-artifact](real-artifact.md); unavailable execution leaves the claim unverified.
  - Proposal-only work: verify relevant proposal states/interactions; leave the product unchanged.
  - Changed exports, shared logic, guards or normalization: inspect consumers and sibling paths and verify affected behavior. Use impact-map/sibling-path-map when useful.
- Reuse evidence only when its relevant implementation, inputs, environment, requirements and coverage still match. Shared dependency changes can invalidate screen checks without screen-file edits; an old screenshot alone proves no freshness. Exact restoration can retain unaffected evidence when equivalence is established, but does not replace repair reproduction. Uncertain applicability or an explicitly required fresh check needs a current check.
- A later edit does not invalidate every earlier result. Inspect what the edit affects: a handoff wording/format change normally leaves code-behavior evidence valid; documentation used as executable input may not. Reuse valid results and run the checks required for the actual change, including repo verification/diff inspection for narrow corrections. Do not rerun unrelated behavior suites solely because a document or report was edited. Complete missing or affected checks; do not build a new recorder or repeat checks merely to copy already available outputs into a report. State reused results as reused, never freshly executed. No new ledger is required.
- Review correctness, cause-level repair, compatibility, component reuse, duplication, responsibilities, boundary validation and meaningful tests using review-diff and its code-quality reference. Passing tests do not establish review; review does not establish behavior. Use independent review when scope/risk warrants it, not for every edit.
- Report each outcome as passed, failed, unverified or needs decision. Missing capability, skipped/stale evidence and unresolved expectations cannot pass. A labeled reconstructed baseline can establish behavior, not an earlier pre-action procedure; review cannot retroactively authorize an out-of-scope act.
- Complete only when every required outcome has valid passing evidence and no known defect or unresolved decision prevents it. An out-of-scope defect can block success without expanding authority. Return to unfinished actions, not completed stages; otherwise report the concrete partial result and gap. Stopping is not success.
- Inspect final outputs, preserve needed evidence and clean up task-created resources. Show checked changed screens before an authorized push. Follow repo local-commit/handoff rules; workers do not take over main Git ownership. Read-only work needs bounded findings, not commits. External actions still require authority.
